description: Eight unmodified operational facts selected on 2026-09-04. Timestamps are recording times; payload.date, where present, is the reported event date. This is an excerpt, not a current health assessment. Unresolved references are retained.

payload.name: gitlab-oom-ssh-banner-2026-04-20
payload.message: GitLab VM (3.8GB RAM, no swap) ran out of memory: gitaly consumed 3.3GB leaving <140MB for OS + sshd. Symptom was TCP handshake succeeding (nc -zv OK) but SSH banner exchange stalling — caused by fork failure from memory starvation, not a network/auth issue. Fix: docker restart gitlab freed 3.0GB, container healthy within ~60s. Long-term fix identified but not yet applied: add swap or increase VM RAM from 4GB to 6GB.

payload.name: ssh-banner-stall-is-memory-starvation
payload.message: On a git/SSH host, if `nc -zv` succeeds (TCP handshake OK) but the SSH banner exchange stalls or hangs, suspect memory starvation causing fork failure rather than network or auth problems. Diagnose with `free -h` on the VM and `docker stats` on the container; restarting the memory-starved container is often sufficient to recover.

payload.name: dev-vm-tmp-tmpfs-wedge-2026-04-28
payload.message: dev VM's /tmp is tmpfs sized at 1.5GB on a 3GB VM. Receiving a 2.2GB scp into /tmp consumed all available memory and wedged sshd. Emergency fix: 2GB /swapfile provisioned inline (fallocate/mkswap/swapon, persisted in fstab). Root-cause fix: bumped VM RAM from 3072 to 6144 MB in terraform/vm-dev.tf; the swap stays as belt-and-suspenders.

payload.name: monitor-alert-selector-blindness-2026-07-12
payload.message: Both Prometheus and Grafana HostDown rules query job=node while the live job is node-exporter; DockerDaemonDown queries nonexistent job=docker. Whole-host and Docker-daemon failure rules are inert. Grafana owns Telegram while Prometheus has no Alertmanager, so alert evaluation/ownership also needs consolidation.

payload.name: media-root-disk-full-2026-07-22
payload.message: Jellyfin crash-looped on media (192.168.1.40) with exit 139: its startup guard refuses to boot below 2GiB free on /config/data. Root cause: unbounded /var/log/journal grew to 3.1G on a 32G root disk (95% full, 1.7G free), no SystemMaxUse cap set. journald had regrown after a prior 2026-05 cleanup (docs/operations/homelab-audit-2026-05-24.md flagged 91% full and recommended a bump) since the fix then was only a one-time vacuum, not a durable cap.

payload.name: media-root-disk-bump-2026-07-22
payload.message: Bumped media VM (vmid 302) root disk 32G -> 50G: qm resize on pve-main (LVM, online), growpart /dev/sda 1 + resize2fs /dev/sda1 inside the VM (no reboot needed). terraform/vm-media.tf disk size updated to 50 for consistency (disk changes are in lifecycle.ignore_changes so terraform plan shows no drift — the .tf value only matters for VM recreation from scratch).

payload.name: journald-size-cap-provisioning
payload.message: systemd-journald has no default disk cap; on flat-compose VMs with small (20-32G) root disks this silently fills the disk over months (seen on media and on runner-01/runner-02, see practice/uncapped-docker-json-file-logging). Fix pattern: drop /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/00-size-cap.conf with SystemMaxUse=1G + SystemKeepFree=2G, both live (systemctl restart systemd-journald) and baked into the VM's cloud-init write_files (proxmox/vm-media.yml) so a re-provisioned VM inherits the cap instead of re-discovering this the hard way. Not yet applied to other VMs' cloud-init — only media so far.

payload.name: journald-fleet-cap-rollout-2026-07-22
payload.message: Rolled out the media journald-cap fix (practice/journald-size-cap-provisioning) fleet-wide: 13/14 guest VMs got a live /etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/00-size-cap.conf (SystemMaxUse=1G/SystemKeepFree=2G standard, 300M/800M on the 10G-disk runners) applied via kaygee sudo (deploy's sudoers is scoped narrower than kaygee's NOPASSWD:ALL on most hosts) plus the same block baked into each proxmox/vm-*.yml cloud-init and re-uploaded to the correct Proxmox node's snippet storage (pve-main/pve-nas/pve-dev — vm-runner.yml uploaded to both pve-main and pve-nas since runner-01/02 live on different nodes). Pre-fix journal sizes ranged 1-4GB uncapped on every host; dev was at 96% root-disk full (811M free, worse than media's incident) and infra at 88% (3.7G free) — both now have headroom back (dev ~1.8G free, infra ~5.8G free). hermes (192.168.1.52) was unreachable (ssh timeout) — cloud-init updated and snippet uploaded to pve-dev, but the live journald.conf.d drop-in was NOT applied; needs a manual pass once it's back up. commission (vmid 407) and homeassistant (HAOS) were out of scope — commission has no live VM yet (config-only stub), HAOS isn't part of this repo's cloud-init/docker-compose fleet.
